summary: The proof is mathematically sound under the locked-problem hypotheses invoked in the candidate. The primary arXiv source, Averkov and Weismantel, Theorem 1.1, states h(R^n x Z^d)=(n+1)2^d, so coordinate permutation gives h(Z x R^2)=6. The finite-family Helly contrapositive is applied correctly, the outward halfspace perturbation is justified by continuity from above of the finite measure, both Helly-subfamily cases have the stated cardinality bounds, and subadditivity makes the cases r<=4 automatic when T>0.
